question: How can error feedback and gradient tracking mechanisms be integrated into federated learning to mitigate the prediction performance degradation caused by high-ratio lossy gradient compression?

source_paper.title: Gradient Compression and Correlation Driven Federated Learning for Wireless Traffic Prediction

main_idea.headline: A novel federated learning algorithm integrates gradient compression and correlation-driven personalized aggregation to minimize communication overhead and capture spatial dependencies in wireless traffic prediction.
contributions: Introduces gradient sparsification into federated wireless traffic prediction to significantly reduce the communication load between local clients and the central server.
Incorporates error feedback and gradient tracking mechanisms to mitigate the performance degradation typically caused by lossy gradient compression.

Designs three personalized model aggregation strategies (k-relevant, delta-threshold, and all-correlated) derived from gradient correlation matrices to capture the distinct spatial dependencies among local clients.

Provides empirical evidence on real-world datasets showing the method improves communication efficiency by up to two orders of magnitude over state-of-the-art baselines without compromising prediction accuracy.

source_paper.problem: While federated learning allows edge nodes to collaboratively train wireless traffic prediction models without sharing raw data, it still incurs heavy communication overhead from frequent gradient exchanges. Additionally, traditional federated aggregation methods fail to capture the complex spatial dependencies and heterogeneous traffic patterns across different geographic locations, often leading to suboptimal or degraded prediction performance when client data distributions diverge.

source_paper.title: MuQ: Self-Supervised Music Representation Learning With Mel Residual Vector Quantization

main_idea.headline: MuQ is a self-supervised music representation learning model that predicts tokens generated by a novel Mel Residual Vector Quantization (Mel-RVQ) to efficiently and stably capture both semantic and acoustic information.
contributions: Introduces MuQ, a self-supervised music representation model that achieves state-of-the-art performance across various downstream music understanding tasks.
Proposes Mel Residual Vector Quantization (Mel-RVQ), a lightweight tokenizer that directly quantizes the Mel spectrum using a single linear layer to improve training stability and efficiency.

source_paper.title: Semantics-Guided Diffusion for Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding in Wireless Image Transmission

main_idea.headline: A semantics-guided diffusion framework for deep joint source-channel coding leverages semantic side information for accurate channel denoising and dynamically adapts to varying channel conditions without pilot transmissions.
contributions: Extracts and transmits inherent semantic information, such as text descriptions and edge maps, to guide the diffusion model towards semantics-aligned channel denoising.
Introduces a pilot-free channel estimation method combined with a continuous timestep matching approach to dynamically adapt the diffusion model to slow fading channels.
Develops a training-free, water-filling-inspired denoising strategy that enables the diffusion model to effectively handle symbol-level noise variations in fast fading channels.

source_paper.problem: Integrating diffusion models into deep joint source-channel coding for wireless image transmission introduces two major challenges: the inherent randomness of diffusion models can destroy key semantic details during denoising, and adapting these models to varying channel conditions typically requires explicit channel state information obtained through costly pilot transmissions. Solving this matters because overcoming these limitations enables high-fidelity, semantics-aligned image reconstruction even under extremely poor or rapidly fluctuating channel conditions without incurring heavy signaling overhead.

source_paper.title: The Prompt Alchemist: Automated LLM-Tailored Prompt Optimization for Test Case Generation

main_idea.headline: MAPS is an automated prompt optimization method that generates LLM-tailored prompts for test case generation by integrating diversity-guided prompt generation, failure-driven rule induction, and domain contextual knowledge extraction.
contributions: A diversity-guided prompt generation module that explores varied modification paths to prevent the optimization process from converging to local optima.

question: How can diffusion transformer architectures and training strategies be enhanced to accelerate convergence speeds and reduce the high computational costs of experimental iterations?

source_paper.title: Reconstruction vs. Generation: Taming Optimization Dilemma in Latent Diffusion Models

main_idea.headline: Aligning the latent space of visual tokenizers with pre-trained vision foundation models resolves the optimization dilemma between reconstruction and generation in latent diffusion models.
contributions: Introducing the Vision Foundation model alignment Loss (VF Loss), a plug-and-play module that uses marginal cosine similarity and marginal distance matrix similarity to regularize high-dimensional latent spaces.
Developing VA-VAE, a visual tokenizer that maintains high reconstruction capacity while structuring the latent space to be more uniform and generation-friendly.
Designing LightningDiT, an enhanced Diffusion Transformer architecture that integrates advanced training strategies and architectural improvements to maximize training efficiency.

Demonstrating empirically that foundation model alignment enables an over 21-fold convergence speedup and achieves state-of-the-art generation fidelity without requiring additional diffusion training compute.

source_paper.problem: Latent diffusion models face a fundamental optimization dilemma when scaling visual tokenizers: increasing the per-token feature dimension improves image reconstruction details but severely degrades generation performance. Consequently, systems must either settle for low-dimensional tokenizers that produce visual artifacts due to information loss, or employ high-dimensional tokenizers that require prohibitively large diffusion models and massive computational costs to converge. This conflict arises from the inherent difficulty of learning unconstrained high-dimensional latent spaces from scratch, limiting the upper bound of generation quality and efficiency.

source_paper.title: EnerVerse: Envisioning Embodied Future Space for Robotics Manipulation

main_idea.headline: EnerVerse is a generative robotics foundation model that predicts 4D embodied future spaces from instructions using a chunk-wise autoregressive video diffusion framework and translates these representations into physical actions.
contributions: A chunk-wise autoregressive diffusion architecture with sparse contextual memory capable of long-term grounding.
A multi-view diffusion generator that endows the model with a 3D spatial prior that improves performance even under single-camera deployments.
A 4D Gaussian Splatting-based data flywheel that supplies geometry-consistent multi-view training data to reduce the sim-to-real gap.

source_paper.problem: Robotic manipulation requires accurate predictions of future states in a 3D, temporally interconnected physical environment. Existing approaches that adapt 2D video generation models to robotics struggle with motion ambiguity and 3D grounding because they lack a true spatial understanding. Additionally, acquiring the precisely calibrated multi-camera data needed to learn these 3D priors is prohibitively expensive and labor-intensive, making it difficult to bridge the sim-to-real gap.

source_paper.title: MambaHSI: Spatial–Spectral Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification

main_idea.headline: MambaHSI is an image-level hyperspectral image classification framework based on state space models that simultaneously models long-range spatial interactions with linear complexity and adaptively integrates continuous spectral information.
contributions: Introduction of the first image-level hyperspectral image classification model based on State Space Models, enabling end-to-end processing of the entire image to capture long-range dependencies with linear computational complexity.
Design of a spatial Mamba block that extracts fine-grained, pixel-level spatial features across the whole image.
Development of a spectral Mamba block that splits spectral vectors into groups to mine sequential relationships and extract discriminative spectral features.

source_paper.problem: Hyperspectral image classification requires capturing both fine-grained pixel-level details and long-range spatial dependencies. Existing CNN-based methods are limited by their local receptive fields, while Transformer-based methods suffer from quadratic computational complexity, forcing them to rely on patch-level inputs that hinder efficient full-image global modeling. Furthermore, recent state space models applied to this domain either ignore the continuous sequential nature of spectral bands or still rely on patch-based inputs, which introduces redundant computations and restricts the model's ability to fully exploit global image information.

question: How can the complex architecture of automated issue-resolution systems be streamlined to enable the effective training of open-source models with minimal reasoning steps?

source_paper.title: SWE-Fixer: Training Open-Source LLMs for Effective and Efficient GitHub Issue Resolution

main_idea.headline: SWE-Fixer is a streamlined, open-source pipeline framework that efficiently resolves real-world GitHub issues by decomposing the task into coarse-to-fine code file retrieval and targeted code editing.
contributions: A highly efficient two-step pipeline framework that resolves software issues using open-source models with only two model calls per instance.
A coarse-to-fine retrieval module that combines BM25 with a lightweight language model to accurately isolate defective files from large repository contexts.
A structured code editing module trained via JsonTuning and synthesized Chain-of-Thought data to generate precise, valid code patches.
A rigorously filtered, large-scale training dataset comprising 110K real-world GitHub issues and their corresponding resolution patches.

source_paper.problem: Existing automated systems for resolving real-world GitHub issues rely heavily on complex agentic frameworks and proprietary large language models, making them costly, inefficient, and opaque. Open-source alternatives currently lack the robust autonomous capabilities required for agent-based exploration, and there is a severe scarcity of high-quality, structured training data needed to teach these models how to accurately retrieve defective files and generate valid code patches. This limits the accessibility, reproducibility, and further improvement of LLM-based software engineering tools.

source_paper.title: A General Framework for Inference-time Scaling and Steering of Diffusion Models

main_idea.headline: Feynman-Kac (FK) steering is a flexible, inference-time framework that steers both continuous and discrete diffusion models toward arbitrary reward functions by simulating multiple interacting particles and resampling them at intermediate steps based on potential functions.
contributions: Proposes Feynman-Kac diffusion steering, a particle-based framework for sampling tilted distributions to steer continuous and discrete state-space models with generic reward functions.
Unifies existing particle-based sampling methods as specific instances of FK interacting particle systems and introduces new choices of potentials, samplers, and reward models.
Demonstrates that FK steering with as few as four particles outperforms fine-tuning on prompt fidelity and aesthetic quality for text-to-image models without requiring reward gradients.
Shows that FK steering enables smaller models to outperform larger models using fewer FLOPs and can further improve the performance of already fine-tuned models.
Enables gradient-free control over rare text attributes, significantly outperforming gradient guidance and best-of-n sampling in generating specific attributes like toxicity.

source_paper.problem: Adapting diffusion models to generate samples that conform to user-specified properties or preferences remains a significant challenge. Existing approaches either require expensive fine-tuning that ties the model to a single reward and is prone to mode collapse, or rely on inference-time steering methods that are computationally inefficient (like best-of-n sampling) or restricted to differentiable rewards and continuous-state models (like gradient-based guidance).

question: How can the high implementation complexity of instantaneous port selection in Fluid Antenna Multiple Access (FAMA) be mitigated within a practical 5G NR OFDM framework?

source_paper.title: Downlink OFDM-FAMA in 5G-NR Systems

main_idea.headline: The integration of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access (FAMA) into the 5G New Radio Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) framework enables massive connectivity in broadband multipath channels without requiring transmitter channel state information.
contributions: A downlink OFDM-FAMA architecture that incorporates 5G NR channel coding and OFDM modulation, featuring a port selection mechanism with two training strategies and an interference rejection combining equalizer.

Semi-analytical derivations of the average outage rate, average mutual information, and cutoff rate for OFDM-FAMA, along with an algorithm to approximate the suboptimal fluid antenna system configuration at each user.

Empirical evidence that OFDM-FAMA provides substantial multiplexing gains over fixed-position antenna systems in multipath environments, particularly under robust channel coding and low spectrum efficiency conditions.

source_paper.problem: Extreme massive connectivity for Internet of Things devices requires multiple access schemes that operate efficiently without transmitter channel state information. Fluid Antenna Multiple Access (FAMA) addresses this by dynamically shifting antenna positions to natural interference nulls, but prior FAMA models assume narrowband flat-fading channels. In practical broadband networks, delay spread necessitates Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), creating a critical challenge: an antenna port position that is optimal for one subcarrier may be highly suboptimal for others, making it unknown whether FAMA can actually function effectively in real-world 5G broadband systems.

gaps.target_relation: The target paper integrates FAMA into the 5G NR OFDM framework, enabling port selection based on subframe-average SINR measurements in the frequency domain to reduce implementation complexity.

question: How can integrated sensing and communication be extended to non-terrestrial networks to overcome hardware constraints and enable simultaneous multi-user communication and target location sensing across a multi-satellite LEO constellation?

source_paper.title: Multiple-Satellite Cooperative Information Communication and Location Sensing in LEO Satellite Constellations

main_idea.headline: A dual-function low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation framework that enables simultaneous multi-user information communication and target location sensing by jointly optimizing cooperative communication beamforming and sensing waveforms across multiple satellites.
contributions: A dual-function LEO satellite constellation framework that integrates information communication and location sensing using shared hardware and spectrum.
A closed-form expression for the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) serving as a location sensing metric, derived via a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based direct location sensing algorithm.
A multiple-satellite cooperative design that jointly optimizes communication beamforming and sensing waveforms to improve location sensing accuracy without sacrificing information transmission rates.

source_paper.problem: Traditional LEO satellite systems separate information communication and location sensing onto different platforms due to payload limitations, and existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) research in non-terrestrial networks focuses almost exclusively on individual satellites. When attempting to perform both functions simultaneously across a multi-satellite constellation, severe inter-satellite and inter-functional interference degrades performance. Overcoming this interference within limited wireless resources and highly dynamic environments is necessary to achieve both high-rate communication and high-precision location sensing for 6G air-space-ground integration.

main_idea.headline: This paper presents the first systematic exploration of integrating Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) to enhance their complex reasoning capabilities across diverse auditory modalities.

question: How can Monte Carlo estimation and LLM-as-a-judge be integrated to generate scalable, high-quality training data for Process Reward Models that overcomes the inaccuracies of automated estimation and the high costs of human annotation?

source_paper.title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning

main_idea.headline: A critical analysis of Process Reward Model development reveals the limitations of Monte Carlo estimation and Best-of-N evaluation, leading to a novel consensus filtering mechanism that combines MC estimation with LLM-as-a-judge to train state-of-the-art PRMs.
contributions: Demonstrating that Monte Carlo estimation-based data construction for PRMs yields inferior performance and generalization compared to LLM-as-a-judge and human annotation.

Revealing the biases of relying solely on response-level Best-of-N evaluation, which inflates scores due to flawed reasoning processes that happen to reach correct answers, and advocating for combined response-level and step-level metrics.
Proposing a consensus filtering mechanism that integrates Monte Carlo estimation with LLM-as-a-judge to significantly improve model performance and data efficiency in PRM training.
Releasing state-of-the-art open-source PRMs alongside practical guidelines for future reasoning process supervision.

source_paper.problem: Large Language Models often make logical errors or hallucinate plausible but flawed reasoning steps even when arriving at the correct final mathematical answer. Process Reward Models (PRMs) aim to mitigate this by verifying intermediate steps, but their development is hindered by the high cost of human annotation and the inaccuracies of automated Monte Carlo (MC) estimation. Furthermore, evaluating PRMs solely using Best-of-N (BoN) sampling is misleading, as it fails to penalize models that generate correct answers from incorrect steps, causing PRMs to degrade into outcome-oriented rather than process-oriented evaluators.

question: How can a continual reinforcement learning algorithm be designed to achieve high few-shot performance and rapid adaptation for resource allocation and device scheduling in ever-changing wireless digital twin networks?

source_paper.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning for Digital Twin Synchronization Optimization

main_idea.headline: A continual reinforcement learning-based adaptive resource allocation scheme that optimizes digital twin synchronization by selectively scheduling devices in dynamic wireless networks.
contributions: A digital network twin framework that selectively schedules a subset of devices and optimizes resource block allocation to improve synchronization between physical and virtual systems under limited wireless resources.

Formulation of the device scheduling and resource block allocation problem as a constrained Markov decision process to minimize long-term physical-virtual mismatch while accounting for packet errors and environmental dynamics.
Transformation of the constrained Markov decision process into a dual problem to refine the impacts of resource block constraints on device scheduling strategies.

A continual reinforcement learning algorithm integrating a multi-timescale replay buffer and a modified soft actor-critic agent to quickly adapt to unseen physical system statuses and dynamic network capacities.

source_paper.problem: Continuous synchronization between a physical system and its digital twin requires extensive sensing data transmission, which strains constrained wireless communication resources. Furthermore, the dynamic nature of wireless channels and the unpredictable randomness of physical object states cause synchronization mismatches. Existing resource management methods and standard reinforcement learning approaches struggle to adapt to these unseen environmental dynamics and varying resource constraints without catastrophic forgetting or requiring extensive retraining, leading to degraded digital twin accuracy and delayed state updates.

gaps.limitation: Standard reinforcement learning and digital twin methods struggle with few-shot performance when operating in ever-changing wireless environments.
gaps.evidence_quote: need to be enhanced in regards to their few shot performances with the ever-changing environments
gaps.evidence_source: System Model and Problem Formulation > Problem Formulation
gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces a continual reinforcement learning-based scheme to improve adaptation and resource allocation efficiency in these dynamic environments.

question: How can an LLM serving system dynamically adjust instance batch sizes to prevent inter-token latency violations for interactive requests caused by high-throughput optimizations?

source_paper.title: Hierarchical Autoscaling for Large Language Model Serving with Chiron

main_idea.headline: Chiron is a hierarchical autoscaler for large language model serving that optimizes resource utilization and service-level objective attainment by applying local and global backpressure metrics.
contributions: A local autoscaler that dynamically adjusts instance batch sizes using a combined latency and throughput backpressure metric to prevent inter-token latency violations.
A global autoscaler that multiplexes interactive and batch requests by scaling instances based on queue waiting time estimates and interactive over-provisioning levels.
A request grouping mechanism that clusters batch requests with similar time-to-first-token deadlines to minimize scaling hysteresis.

source_paper.problem: Large language model serving workloads consist of both interactive requests with strict latency constraints and batch requests with relaxed deadlines. Existing autoscalers do not differentiate between these request types, leading them to enforce static batch size limits and immediately scale up instances upon the arrival of batch requests. This lack of service-level objective awareness results in excessive scaling churn, suboptimal throughput, and severe resource under-utilization across the cluster.

gaps.limitation: High throughput optimizations lead to increased request preemptions and inflated inter-token latency (ITL) for interactive requests beyond SLO values.
gaps.evidence_quote: they also lead to increased request preemptions and inflate the inter-token latency for interactive requests beyond the SLO value
gaps.target_relation: Chiron applies local and global backpressure metrics to optimize SLO attainment and resource utilization, mitigating the latency inflation caused by high-throughput batching.

gaps.limitation: The use of a first-come-first-serve (FCFS) scheduling policy results in head-of-line (HOL) blocking.
gaps.evidence_quote: adopts continuous batching and a first-come-first-serve (FCFS) scheduling policy that suffers from head-of-line (HOL) blocking
gaps.target_relation: Chiron addresses HOL blocking through its hierarchical autoscaling framework and scheduling optimizations.

question: How can diverse multi-modal prompts, such as images, videos, texts, and humming, be parsed into a unified projection space to guide generalized symbolic music generation?

source_paper.title: XMusic: Towards a Generalized and Controllable Symbolic Music Generation Framework

main_idea.headline: XMusic is a generalized symbolic music generation framework that parses diverse multi-modal prompts into a unified projection space to generate emotionally controllable, high-quality MIDI compositions.
contributions: A multi-modal controllable framework, XMusic, that supports images, videos, texts, tags, and humming as input prompts for symbolic music generation.
A parsing module, XProjector, that maps heterogeneous multi-modal prompts into specific symbolic music elements like emotions, genres, rhythms, and notes to act as control signals.
A music composer, XComposer, comprising a Generator that creates music using an enhanced symbolic representation and a Selector that evaluates and filters outputs via a multi-task learning scheme.
XMIDI, a large-scale dataset of 108,023 MIDI files annotated with precise emotion and genre labels.

source_paper.problem: Current symbolic music generation models cannot seamlessly integrate diverse multi-modal prompts—such as images, videos, texts, and humming—into a single framework. They also struggle to exert fine-grained control over musical emotions, lack mechanisms to automatically assess and filter the quality of generated outputs, and are constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, accurately annotated symbolic music datasets. Solving these issues is critical for enabling users to intuitively and reliably generate high-quality, emotionally resonant music tailored to specific multimedia contexts or creative intents.

gaps.limitation: The method specifies the emotion tag token only at the beginning of the entire music piece, which limits the precision of emotional control.

gaps.target_relation: XMusic places the Tag token at the beginning of each bar to ensure the generated music adheres more closely to the specified tag and allows for bar-by-bar emotional fine-tuning.

gaps.limitation: The integration of diverse multi-modal prompt types within a single generative model remains unexplored in existing methods like EMOPIA.
gaps.evidence_quote: Despite considerable advancements in the field of conditional symbolic music generation, the integration of diverse prompt types (such as images, videos, texts, tags, and humming) within a single generative model remains unexplored.
gaps.target_relation: XMusic parses diverse multi-modal prompts into a unified projection space to generate music within a single generalized framework.

gaps.limitation: CMT is restricted to video-based prompts and lacks the capability to integrate multiple prompt modalities like text, images, and humming within a single generative framework.
gaps.evidence_quote: the integration of diverse prompt types (such as images, videos, texts, tags, and humming) within a single generative model remains unexplored.
gaps.target_relation: XMusic addresses this by parsing diverse multi-modal prompts into a unified projection space to enable generalized symbolic music generation.

gaps.limitation: The motion extraction method (optical flow) associated with the CMT-inspired rhythmic control approach has high computational complexity.

gaps.target_relation: XMusic replaces optical flow with a more efficient Patch Aggregation (PA) method to model video motion for rhythmic control.

question: Can an autoregressive vision-language-action model match the performance of diffusion-based policies on complex dexterous tasks while requiring significantly less training compute?

source_paper.title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models

main_idea.headline: A novel compression-based tokenization scheme, FAST, utilizes the discrete cosine transform to enable efficient training of autoregressive vision-language-action models on high-frequency, dexterous robot data.
contributions: Introduces FAST, an action tokenization algorithm that compresses continuous robot action chunks using the discrete cosine transform followed by byte-pair encoding.
Releases FAST+, a universal off-the-shelf robot action tokenizer trained on one million real robot action trajectories spanning diverse embodiments, action spaces, and control frequencies.
Demonstrates that FAST enables autoregressive VLAs to match the performance of state-of-the-art diffusion models on complex dexterous tasks while reducing training time by up to 5x.
Trains the first language-conditioned generalist manipulation policy on the DROID dataset capable of zero-shot evaluation in completely unseen environments.

source_paper.problem: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models require continuous robot actions to be discretized into tokens. Standard tokenization methods rely on naive per-dimension, per-timestep binning, which produces highly correlated tokens when applied to high-frequency control data. This redundancy drastically reduces the marginal information of each token, causing models to fall into poor local optima (such as simply copying the previous action) and making it exceedingly difficult to learn complex, dexterous skills from high-frequency robot data.

gaps.limitation: The diffusion-based decoding approach used in pi_0 is computationally expensive to train and has slower convergence compared to autoregressive methods.
gaps.evidence_quote: while being significantly more compute efficient to train
gaps.target_relation: The FAST tokenization scheme enables autoregressive training of vision-language-action models, which matches the performance of diffusion-based models like pi_0 while requiring significantly less training compute and time.

question: How can stereo matching models efficiently process large disparity distributions in high-resolution images without incurring the prohibitive memory costs associated with large 3D convolution kernels?

source_paper.title: FoundationStereo: Zero-Shot Stereo Matching

main_idea.headline: FoundationStereo is a foundation model for stereo depth estimation that achieves strong zero-shot generalization across diverse domains without requiring per-domain fine-tuning.
contributions: A zero-shot generalizable stereo matching model that rivals fine-tuned prior works and significantly outperforms existing methods on in-the-wild data.
A large-scale, high-fidelity synthetic dataset of one million stereo pairs, featuring an automatic self-curation pipeline to remove ambiguous samples.
A Side-Tuning Adapter (STA) that integrates internet-scale semantic and geometric priors from a pre-trained monocular depth estimation model into the stereo setup.
An Attentive Hybrid Cost Filtering (AHCF) module comprising 3D Axial-Planar Convolutions and a Disparity Transformer to enable long-range context reasoning over the disparity space.

source_paper.problem: Deep stereo matching models typically require per-domain fine-tuning to achieve competitive results and struggle to generalize to unseen, in-the-wild scenarios. This lack of zero-shot generalization, caused by architectures that fail to capture long-range context and a reliance on small or impoverished training datasets, prevents the deployment of stereo matching algorithms as robust, off-the-shelf foundation models.

gaps.limitation: The 3D convolutions with small kernels (3x3x3) used in IGEV-Stereo struggle to model large disparity distributions in high-resolution images, and increasing the kernel size is memory-prohibitive.

gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces Axial-Planar Convolution (APC) filtering to efficiently handle large disparity ranges without the unmanageable memory usage of large 3D kernels.

question: How can the global cross-modal relevance and local temporal alignment between generated music and video content be objectively evaluated to overcome the limitations of subjective assessments?

source_paper.title: GVMGen: A General Video-to-Music Generation Model with Hierarchical Attentions

main_idea.headline: GVMGen is a general video-to-music generation model that employs hierarchical spatial and temporal attentions to implicitly align visual and musical features, enabling the generation of diverse, high-fidelity audio tracks for various video styles.
contributions: A novel video-to-music generation architecture (GVMGen) that uses spatial self-attention, spatial cross-attention, and temporal cross-attention to implicitly extract and align cross-modal features without relying on predefined rules or text descriptions.

question: How can scale drift be prevented and smooth depth transitions maintained when performing depth estimation on arbitrarily long video sequences?

source_paper.title: Video Depth Anything: Consistent Depth Estimation for Super-Long Videos

main_idea.headline: Video Depth Anything adapts a pre-trained image depth foundation model using an efficient spatial-temporal head and a novel inference strategy to achieve temporally consistent depth estimation for arbitrarily long videos.
contributions: A lightweight spatial-temporal head that integrates temporal attention layers into the DPT head to capture inter-frame relationships without altering the frozen image encoder.

A Temporal Gradient Matching loss that enforces temporal consistency by matching depth changes between adjacent frames to ground truth changes, eliminating the need for optical flow or geometric priors.
A segment-wise inference strategy that combines overlapping frame interpolation and key-frame referencing to prevent scale drift and ensure smooth depth transitions across super-long videos.
A joint training approach utilizing both labeled video sequences and unlabeled static images to maintain the zero-shot generalization capabilities of the base image depth model.

source_paper.problem: State-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models are designed for static images and produce flickering, temporally inconsistent depth maps when applied to videos. Existing methods to enforce temporal consistency either rely on error-prone geometric priors like optical flow, or utilize computationally expensive video diffusion models that are restricted to short video clips and cannot efficiently scale to super-long videos.

gaps.limitation: The model is designed for static images and lacks temporal consistency, resulting in flickering and motion blur when applied to video sequences.
gaps.evidence_quote: they are mainly designed for static images and suffer from flickering and motion blur in videos
gaps.target_relation: The target paper adapts the pre-trained model with a spatial-temporal head and a segment-wise inference strategy to ensure temporal consistency for arbitrarily long videos.

source_paper.title: InternVideo2.5: Empowering Video MLLMs with Long and Rich Context Modeling

main_idea.headline: InternVideo2.5 enhances video Multimodal Large Language Models by explicitly modeling long and rich multimodal context through adaptive hierarchical token compression and task preference optimization.
contributions: A unified schema for Long and Rich Context (LRC) modeling that combines hierarchical token compression (HiCo) and task preference optimization (TPO) to enhance MLLM memory and focus.
InternVideo2.5, a new video MLLM that extends video memory capacity by at least six times and achieves state-of-the-art performance on short and long video understanding benchmarks.

question: How can a recurrent state-update mechanism enable continuous, online dense 3D reconstruction from multi-view image streams without requiring offline global alignment?

source_paper.title: Continuous 3D Perception Model with Persistent State

main_idea.headline: A stateful recurrent 3D perception framework continuously updates a persistent internal state from an image stream to perform online dense 3D reconstruction and infer unobserved scene regions.
contributions: A recurrent state-update and state-readout mechanism continuously integrates new image observations into a persistent 3D scene state to predict metric-scale pointmaps and camera poses online.
A virtual camera querying approach infers the 3D geometry and color of unobserved scene regions by probing the persistent state with a raymap.

A flexible formulation seamlessly processes varying numbers of images, unstructured photo collections, and monocular videos of both static and dynamic scenes without requiring known camera intrinsics or extrinsics.

source_paper.problem: Traditional 3D reconstruction methods typically operate from scratch for each new scene, struggling with sparse observations, dynamic objects, and degenerate camera motion. Meanwhile, recent learning-based approaches often require offline global alignment, are limited to static scenes, or depend on known camera parameters. This creates a need for a continuous, online perception system capable of incrementally building and refining a 3D scene representation from arbitrary image streams while also inferring unobserved regions.

source_paper.title: VideoLLaMA 3: Frontier Multimodal Foundation Models for Image and Video Understanding

main_idea.headline: VideoLLaMA 3 is a vision-centric multimodal foundation model that achieves state-of-the-art image and video understanding by leveraging high-quality image-text data and dynamic vision tokenization.
contributions: Introduces VideoLLaMA3, an advanced multimodal foundation model that achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of image and video understanding benchmarks.

question: How can we establish a comprehensive multi-task training and evaluation framework to effectively assess and improve the performance of Speech Understanding Language Models in non-English languages, specifically Chinese?

source_paper.title: OSUM: Advancing Open Speech Understanding Models with Limited Resources in Academia

main_idea.headline: OSUM is an open-source Speech Understanding Language Model that achieves strong multi-task performance under constrained academic resources by combining a Whisper encoder with a Qwen2 LLM and employing an efficient ASR+X training strategy.
contributions: Develops OSUM, an open-source SULM integrating a Whisper encoder and Qwen2 LLM to support eight distinct speech tasks.
Introduces an ASR+X multi-task training paradigm that concurrently optimizes automatic speech recognition alongside target tasks to accelerate modality alignment and reduce resource consumption.
Incorporates Speaking Style Recognition (SSR) as a novel task to improve contextual comprehension and enable more natural speech-based interactions.
Constructs a comprehensive suite of internal multi-task test sets tailored for Chinese speech understanding to complement existing public English benchmarks.
Releases the complete data processing pipeline, training methodologies, and model weights to promote transparency and accessibility for academic researchers.

question: How can we construct a large-scale human preference dataset and an annotated benchmark that accurately reflect user preferences for modern, high-fidelity video generation models?

source_paper.title: Improving Video Generation with Human Feedback

main_idea.headline: A comprehensive framework for aligning modern flow-based video generation models with human preferences using a new large-scale preference dataset, a multi-dimensional reward model, and tailored flow-matching alignment algorithms.
contributions: Constructs a 182k-sized, multi-dimensional human preference dataset generated by 12 modern text-to-video models.
Develops VideoReward, a multi-dimensional video reward model that utilizes a Bradley-Terry-with-Ties loss and specific token positioning to disentangle multi-attribute signals.
Creates VideoGen-RewardBench, a benchmark of 26.5k annotated video pairs for evaluating reward models on modern video generation outputs.
Derives three alignment algorithms for rectified flow models: Flow-DPO, Flow-RWR, and Flow-NRG.
Demonstrates that using a constant KL penalty in Flow-DPO prevents the reward hacking and visual artifacts caused by timestep-dependent schedules.

source_paper.problem: Modern text-to-video models frequently produce videos with unstable motion, imperfect text-video alignment, and poor adherence to human preferences. Applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to address these issues is currently bottlenecked by the lack of reliable reward signals—since existing preference datasets are based on outdated, low-resolution models—and the difficulty of adapting existing diffusion-based alignment algorithms to the rectified flow architectures used by state-of-the-art video generators.

gaps.limitation: The preference datasets used are based on early, low-resolution T2V models that produce short, artifact-laden clips.
gaps.evidence_quote: were primarily built on early, low-resolution T2V models that produced short, artifact-laden clips
gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces a new large-scale preference dataset specifically targeting modern, high-fidelity, and long-range video generation models.

gaps.limitation: Alignment methods like DPO and RWR are applied to diffusion-based video models rather than modern flow-based architectures.
gaps.evidence_quote: extend DPO/RWR to diffusion-based video models using old generation models or image-level rewards
gaps.target_relation: The target paper extends DPO to flow-based video generation by proposing Flow-DPO.

gaps.limitation: The preference dataset is composed of short, low-resolution clips from early T2V models, which do not reflect the quality or user preferences associated with modern high-fidelity video generation.
gaps.evidence_quote: Existing preference datasets [THIS_PAPER] [he2024videoscore] [liu2024videodpo] [xu2024visionreward] were collected on earlier T2V models that produced short, low-resolution clips.
gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces a new large-scale preference dataset featuring modern T2V models with higher resolutions and longer clips to better align with modern capabilities.

gaps.limitation: The alignment methodology is designed for diffusion-based models and does not address the specific mechanisms of modern flow-based video generation architectures.
gaps.evidence_quote: All of these works use Diffusion-DPO or Diffusion-RWR and focus on aligning diffusion-based video generation models

main_idea.headline: OSTQuant improves large language model quantization by employing learnable orthogonal and scaling transformations to optimize data distributions across the entire quantization space.

question: How can adversarial machine learning techniques be adapted to automatically generate structured and targeted malicious payloads for evaluating Web Application Firewalls?

source_paper.title: WAFBooster: Automatic Boosting of WAF Security Against Mutated Malicious Payloads

main_idea.headline: WAFBooster is a black-box, learning-based framework that automatically exposes unknown mutated malicious payloads against Web Application Firewalls and generates robust signatures to fortify their security rules.
contributions: An automated framework that boosts Web Application Firewall security by generating malicious payloads and corresponding signatures without requiring attack-specific expert knowledge.

A payload generation pipeline that combines shadow model training to imitate the target firewall, an RNN-based sequence generator to create mutated payloads, and a semantic similarity-based payload corrector to ensure the generated payloads remain valid and executable.

An automated signature generation technique that identifies critical payload substrings using four scoring functions, clusters them via edit distance, and produces simplified regular expressions to update security rules while minimizing false alarms.

source_paper.problem: Traditional Web Application Firewalls rely on predefined security policies that struggle to detect ever-evolving, mutated attack payloads designed to bypass their defenses. source_paper.title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation

main_idea.headline: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation (CoRAG) is a framework that trains language models to dynamically retrieve and reason over information step-by-step before generating a final answer.
contributions: A framework that explicitly trains language models to perform iterative, step-by-step retrieval and reasoning.
An automated rejection sampling method that augments standard QA datasets with intermediate retrieval chains without requiring manual annotation.
A set of test-time decoding strategies, including best-of-N sampling and tree search, designed to scale test-time compute by controlling the length and number of retrieval chains.

question: How can over-the-air federated learning systems achieve optimal convergence through direct unbiased gradient estimation and interference elimination using a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), rather than relying on the optimization of loose theoretical upper bounds of the loss function?

source_paper.title: Combating Interference for Over-the-Air Federated Learning: A Statistical Approach via RIS

main_idea.headline: This paper proposes a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered robust aggregation framework for over-the-air federated learning that achieves statistical interference elimination and unbiased gradient estimation without requiring instantaneous channel state information at the transmitter.
contributions: Establishes performance objectives tailored for interference suppression in wireless federated learning systems, focusing on achieving unbiased gradient estimation and minimizing its mean square error.

Introduces the concept of phase-manipulated favorable propagation and channel hardening enabled by RIS for over-the-air federated learning, which statistically eliminates interference without instantaneous channel state information at the transmitter.
Proposes two robust aggregation schemes with distinct power control and RIS phase shift designs that both guarantee unbiased gradient estimation in the presence of interference.

Derives accurate closed-form expressions for the mean square error of gradient estimation, demonstrating that computation and interference errors diminish by an order of O(1/N) where N is the number of RIS elements.

Theoretically analyzes the federated learning convergence of the proposed schemes, proving a convergence rate of O(1/sqrt{T}) and showing that the ideal interference-free convergence rate can be asymptotically achieved by increasing the number of RIS elements.

source_paper.problem: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) significantly enhances the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning by aggregating local updates via analog waveform superposition. However, this analog aggregation makes the system highly vulnerable to both unintentional interference (e.g., multi-cell or multi-task interference) and intentional malicious attacks. Existing solutions typically require deploying expensive large-scale antenna arrays or sacrificing the bandwidth-saving benefits of AirComp, creating a need for a cost-effective, robust framework that suppresses interference while preserving the efficiency of over-the-air aggregation.

gaps.limitation: The theoretical upper bound for the loss function used as an optimization objective is not strictly tight and deviates from the actual loss function, hindering optimal convergence.
gaps.evidence_quote: the derived upper bound is not strictly tight and can exhibit notable deviation from the true loss function
gaps.target_relation: Instead of optimizing a loose upper bound, the target paper focuses on directly achieving the underlying conditions for convergence—unbiased gradient estimation and interference elimination—through RIS and transceiver design.

source_paper.title: PATCH: Empowering Large Language Model with Programmer-Intent Guidance and Collaborative-Behavior Simulation for Automatic Bug Fixing

main_idea.headline: PATCH is a novel stage-wise framework that enhances LLM-based automatic bug fixing by augmenting buggy code with dependence context and programmer intent, and simulating the collaborative bug management process using multiple LLM agents.
contributions: Proposing a stage-wise framework that decomposes bug fixing into reporting, diagnosis, generation, and verification stages handled by distinct LLM agents.
Augmenting buggy code inputs with class- and repository-level dependence contexts and programmer intent derived from commit messages to better guide patch generation.
Constructing and releasing a meta-rich bug-fixing benchmark that pairs real-world bugs with their corresponding dependence contexts and intent information.
Releasing the complete replication package and source code of the PATCH framework to support future research.

source_paper.problem: Current LLM-based bug-fixing approaches treat debugging as a single-step process and only provide the isolated buggy code snippet as input. This fails to capture the cross-file dependencies, programmer intent, and collaborative multi-step reasoning (such as diagnosis and peer review) required to effectively resolve complex software bugs, leading to low patch accuracy.

venue_info.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

question: How can a tri-hybrid MIMO architecture utilize digital and analog precoding to compensate for the coupled phase-magnitude responses and waveguide power decay inherent in dynamic metasurface antennas?

source_paper.title: Embracing Reconfigurable Antennas in the Tri-Hybrid MIMO Architecture for 6G and Beyond

main_idea.headline: A novel tri-hybrid MIMO architecture integrates low-power reconfigurable antennas with traditional digital and analog precoding to drastically improve the energy efficiency of extremely large-scale MIMO systems.
contributions: Formulation of the tri-hybrid MIMO architecture, which adds a third layer of electromagnetic precoding via reconfigurable antennas to conventional digital and analog processing domains.

Categorization and evaluation of state-of-the-art reconfigurable antenna technologies—including metasurfaces, parasitic element-assisted arrays, and structurally reconfigurable arrays—for integration into hybrid systems.
Development of a mathematical system model and a baseline precoding algorithm for a tri-hybrid architecture utilizing dynamic metasurface antennas subject to Lorentzian constraints.

Demonstration that the dynamic metasurface antenna-based tri-hybrid architecture achieves significantly higher energy efficiency than conventional fully-digital, fully-analog, and hybrid MIMO baselines.

source_paper.problem: As MIMO systems scale up for 6G and beyond, hardware complexity and power consumption increase drastically due to the large number of required radio-frequency chains and phase shifters. While hybrid analog-digital architectures mitigate this to some extent, extremely large-scale deployments still suffer from prohibitive energy demands. Energy efficiency is a critical performance indicator for future wireless networks, and without novel transceiver architectures that drastically reduce power consumption, scaling MIMO to the thousands of antennas required for next-generation applications will remain practically infeasible.

question: How can audio large language models be trained to provide natural language descriptions and qualitative analyses of speech quality rather than relying solely on numerical scores?

source_paper.title: Audio Large Language Models Can Be Descriptive Speech Quality Evaluators

main_idea.headline: This paper introduces the first descriptive speech quality evaluation dataset and a token-level distillation method, ALLD, to enable audio large language models to assess and describe speech quality like humans.
contributions: Identifies the inability of current audio LLMs to perceive intrinsic speech quality, establishing the need for descriptive speech evaluation in multimodal agents.
Introduces the first descriptive speech quality evaluation dataset, featuring natural language-based multidimensional analyses and comparative A/B tests derived from authentic human ratings.
Proposes Alignment with LLM Distillation (ALLD), a token-level distillation strategy that aligns audio LLM outputs with an expert LLM to enable end-to-end perception and generation.
Demonstrates that ALLD outperforms state-of-the-art regression models in MOS prediction and A/B testing while mitigating language capability degradation during audio-text pre-training.

source_paper.problem: Current audio large language models can extract semantic content from speech but remain unaware of the intrinsic signal quality, such as distortion, noisiness, or discontinuity. This limitation exists because traditional speech quality evaluation relies on simple numerical scores (like MOS) without descriptive reasoning, and there are no natural language datasets available to teach audio LLMs how to analyze and explain speech quality degradation. Addressing this gap is crucial for building multimodal agents capable of comprehensively perceiving auditory inputs and automating the evaluation of generative audio systems.

gaps.evidence_quote: existing human speech quality datasets consist solely of numerical scores, and do not include any natural language-based descriptions or analyses
gaps.target_relation: The target paper uses the numerical data from the cited work to generate a new dataset of natural language descriptions and proposes a method (ALLD) to enable models to provide qualitative analysis alongside scores.

question: How can harmful fine-tuning data be optimized to reliably degrade a language model's safety alignment while simultaneously evading guardrail moderation?

source_paper.title: Virus: Harmful Fine-tuning Attack for Large Language Models Bypassing Guardrail Moderation

main_idea.headline: The paper introduces Virus, a dual-objective data optimization attack that modifies harmful fine-tuning data to successfully bypass guardrail moderation while effectively degrading the safety alignment of large language models.
contributions: An empirical evaluation demonstrating that while standard guardrail moderation effectively filters unmodified harmful samples, it remains vulnerable to adaptive attacks.
The identification of the gradient mis-match phenomenon, revealing that data optimized solely to bypass moderation loses its ability to compromise the victim model's safety alignment.
The development of Virus, a dual-goal data optimization method that simultaneously minimizes guardrail detection loss and maintains gradient similarity with original harmful data.
The empirical finding that dual-goal optimized data can achieve up to a 100% guardrail leakage ratio while significantly degrading the safety alignment of the fine-tuned LLM.

source_paper.problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) offered through fine-tuning-as-a-service are vulnerable to harmful fine-tuning attacks, where a few malicious examples can compromise the model's safety alignment. While service providers typically deploy guardrail moderation models to filter out harmful training data, it is critical to determine whether these defenses are robust against adaptive adversaries who strategically modify their data to evade detection while retaining the malicious payload.

gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces Virus to provide a more robust and effective dual-objective attack that successfully degrades safety alignment even when guardrail moderation is present, addressing the weakness of benign fine-tuning.

contributions: Introduces a Thinking-LLM-as-a-Judge architecture that separates evaluation Chain-of-Thought into an unconstrained planning phase and a step-by-step execution phase.

question: How can an adaptive decoding framework optimize the trade-off between computational cost and reasoning accuracy to achieve high performance without the extensive sampling budget required by Best-of-N methods?

source_paper.title: Reward-Guided Speculative Decoding for Efficient LLM Reasoning

main_idea.headline: Reward-Guided Speculative Decoding (RSD) accelerates large language model inference by using a process reward model to selectively accept high-quality draft steps, introducing a controlled bias that optimizes the trade-off between computational cost and reasoning accuracy.
contributions: Introduces an adaptive decoding framework that dynamically mixes outputs from a draft and target model guided by a stepwise process reward function.
Formulates a flexible mixture distribution that balances computational efficiency and reasoning accuracy through reward-based weighting and rejection sampling.
Theoretically proves that a threshold-based binary weighting strategy is optimal for maximizing expected reward under a constrained sampling budget.
Demonstrates empirically that reward-guided speculative decoding significantly reduces inference FLOPs while simultaneously improving reasoning accuracy over standard speculative decoding.

source_paper.problem: Sequential token generation in large language models incurs high latency and computational costs, hindering deployment in real-time applications. Existing speculative decoding methods attempt to accelerate this process but enforce strict unbiasedness, meaning they reject high-quality draft tokens that do not exactly match the target model's distribution, which wastes computation and limits efficiency gains in complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.

question: How can reinforcement learning frameworks be designed to optimize large language models for long-term conversational impact and intent discovery rather than immediate, single-turn rewards?

source_paper.title: CollabLLM: From Passive Responders to Active Collaborators

main_idea.headline: CollabLLM is a novel training framework that enhances multiturn human-LLM collaboration by optimizing for long-term conversational impact using Multiturn-aware Rewards derived from collaborative simulation.
contributions: Develops CollabLLM, a reinforcement learning framework that leverages collaborative simulation to estimate the long-term impact of responses via Multiturn-aware Rewards.
Establishes three challenging multiturn tasks (MediumDocEdit-Chat, BigCodeBench-Chat, and MATH-Chat) for training and evaluating collaborative LLMs in simulated environments.
Improves task accuracy by 18.5% and interactivity by 46.3% over strong baselines in simulated environments.
Validates the framework through a large-scale user study with 201 participants, revealing a 17.6% increase in user satisfaction and a 10.4% reduction in task completion time.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization of proactive, intent-seeking behaviors to out-of-domain tasks like ambiguity detection in conversational QA.

source_paper.problem: Real-world users often initiate interactions with imprecise or incomplete requests, requiring iterative refinement to achieve their underlying goals. Standard LLMs, which are typically trained to maximize immediate, single-turn rewards, respond passively to these ambiguous prompts rather than actively seeking clarification. This misalignment leads to inefficient conversations, increased user frustration, and suboptimal task completion, highlighting the critical need for models capable of forward-looking, multiturn collaboration.

main_idea.headline: PRIME is a reinforcement learning framework that leverages implicit process rewards to enable online updates of dense reward models using only outcome labels, bypassing the need for expensive step-level annotations.

question: How can an adaptive continuous entanglement generation protocol be designed to mitigate the decoherence of idle pre-generated pairs stored in quantum memories?

source_paper.title: Design and Simulation of the Adaptive Continuous Entanglement Generation Protocol

main_idea.headline: The Adaptive Continuous entanglement generation Protocol (ACP) minimizes the time-to-serve for quantum network requests by continuously pre-generating entangled pairs in the background using an adaptive neighbor selection scheme.
contributions: An adaptive control mechanism that dynamically updates local probability tables based on historical request paths to guide continuous, background entanglement generation.
An integrated entanglement purification strategy that mitigates the decoherence of idle pre-generated entangled pairs stored in quantum memories.
Architectural extensions to the SeQUeNCe simulator, including a single-heralded entanglement generation protocol that reuses pre-generated pairs and a resource manager for purification policies.

question: How can indirect prompt injection be leveraged to stealthily inflate the inference costs and latency of reasoning language models by forcing excessive hidden reasoning token generation without altering the correctness or coherence of the final user-facing answer?

source_paper.title: OverThink: Slowdown Attacks on Reasoning LLMs

main_idea.headline: This paper introduces OverThink, a novel indirect prompt injection attack that embeds benign decoy tasks into external context to force reasoning language models to generate excessive reasoning tokens, thereby inflating inference costs and latency without altering the final answer.
contributions: Proposes the OverThink attack, which uses context-aware and context-agnostic decoy injections to covertly exhaust reasoning model resources.
Introduces ICL-Evolve, an in-context learning-based optimization algorithm to discover and evolve decoy challenges that maximize reasoning token generation.
Demonstrates the attack's efficacy across multiple state-of-the-art text and multi-modal reasoning models, achieving up to a 46x increase in reasoning tokens.
Evaluates existing defenses such as prompt injection guardrails, filtering, and paraphrasing, revealing their limited effectiveness against the proposed slowdown attacks.

source_paper.problem: Reasoning language models (RLMs) improve performance through inference-time scaling by generating intermediate reasoning tokens, which incur the same financial and computational costs as output tokens. When RLMs process untrusted external data (e.g., via retrieval-augmented generation), they are vulnerable to indirect prompt injections. If an adversary can force the model to over-generate hidden reasoning tokens without altering the final user-facing answer, they can silently inflate API costs, increase latency, and exhaust computational resources, effectively executing a stealthy denial-of-service attack on the deploying application.

gaps.limitation: Prior indirect prompt injection attacks focus on provoking harmful outputs or altering the model's answer, which can be detected by users or safety mechanisms.
gaps.evidence_quote: the adversary's goal is not to provoke harmful output (that can trigger jailbreaking defenses [anthropic2025] [zaremba2025trading]) but to increase the number of reasoning tokens
gaps.evidence_source: Background and Related Work > Related Attacks
gaps.target_relation: The target paper introduces a novel attack vector that inflates inference costs and latency by increasing reasoning tokens while keeping the final answer unchanged and benign.

gaps.limitation: The attack method results in long but incoherent output chains, which makes the attack detectable and undermines the goal of stealthiness.
gaps.evidence_quote: their analysis shows that this can lead to long but incoherent output chains, undermining our objective of answer stealthiness.
gaps.evidence_source: The OverThink Attack > Why is the Attack Hard?
gaps.target_relation: OverThink ensures the final answer remains benign and correct while only inflating the hidden reasoning process, thereby maintaining stealthiness.

main_idea.headline: The paper introduces SmolLM2, a highly performant 1.7-billion-parameter language model trained on 11 trillion tokens using a novel multi-stage data-mixing strategy and newly curated specialized datasets.

question: How can depth-recurrent language models be trained scalably without relying on fixed-point priors or solving direct equilibrium problems?

source_paper.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach

main_idea.headline: A novel language model architecture scales test-time computation by implicitly reasoning in continuous latent space through a depth-recurrent block, bypassing the need to generate discrete chain-of-thought tokens.
contributions: Designs a transformer architecture with a latent depth-recurrent block trained via randomized truncated unrolling to enable arbitrary test-time compute scaling.
Scales the recurrent-depth model to 3.5 billion parameters and 800 billion tokens, demonstrating continuous performance improvements on reasoning benchmarks as test-time compute increases.

Demonstrates that the recurrent architecture naturally supports zero-shot adaptive compute, KV-cache sharing, continuous chain-of-thought, and self-speculative decoding without specialized fine-tuning.
Identifies emergent structured geometric computation patterns in the model's latent space, such as multi-dimensional orbits and directional drifts, that handle complex reasoning tasks.

source_paper.problem: Mainstream approaches to scaling test-time compute rely on generating long chains-of-thought, which requires bespoke training data and consumes massive amounts of memory due to extended context windows. Forcing all internal reasoning to be projected down to discrete verbalized tokens is computationally wasteful and fails to capture complex reasoning that defies verbalization, such as spatial thinking or physical intuition.

gaps.limitation: The training objective in equilibrium models requires solving the 'direct' problem or encoding a fixed-point prior, which lacks the scalability of truncated unrolling.
gaps.evidence_quote: our work suggests that truncated unrolling is a scalable alternative
gaps.target_relation: The target paper replaces the fixed-point/direct-problem training objective with truncated unrolling to provide a more scalable training method for depth-recurrent architectures.

question: To what extent do the vulnerabilities of large language models to a diverse range of tampering attacks lie within a low-dimensional geometric subspace?

source_paper.title: Model Tampering Attacks Enable More Rigorous Evaluations of LLM Capabilities

main_idea.headline: Model tampering attacks, which modify latent activations or weights, provide a more rigorous method than standard input-space attacks for evaluating the worst-case risks and hidden capabilities of large language models.
contributions: Demonstrating that large language model resilience to diverse capability elicitation attacks lies on a low-dimensional robustness subspace.
Showing that the success rates of model tampering attacks correlate with and can empirically predict the success of held-out input-space attacks.
Establishing that few-shot fine-tuning attacks can be used to conservatively over-estimate a model's vulnerability to unforeseen input-space threats.
Revealing that state-of-the-art unlearning methods can be reliably reversed to restore harmful capabilities within 16 steps of fine-tuning.
Releasing a suite of 64 models trained with 8 different methods to unlearn dual-use biology knowledge to facilitate further research.

source_paper.problem: Current risk evaluations for large language models rely primarily on input-space attacks, which are fundamentally limited because the input space is too vast to search exhaustively and adversaries often have access to model weights or fine-tuning APIs. As a result, input-output evaluations only provide a lower bound on a model's worst-case behavior, frequently failing to identify severe vulnerabilities and harmful capabilities before deployment.

gaps.limitation: The investigation of safety brittleness was limited to only two specific types of modifications: pruning and low-rank modifications.
gaps.evidence_quote: Previously [THIS_PAPER] found that a model's vulnerability to pruning and low-rank modifications both relate with the brittleness of its safety fine-tuning. Here, we extend on this finding with more attacks and subspace analysis.
gaps.evidence_source: Experiments > Unlearning Experiments > Model robustness exists on a low-dimensional subspace
gaps.target_relation: The target paper expands the scope of the evaluation by incorporating a wider variety of tampering attacks and performing subspace analysis to understand the geometry of attack successes.

main_idea.headline: ConRFT is a reinforced fine-tuning framework for Vision-Language-Action models that combines offline and online reinforcement learning under a unified consistency-based objective to overcome the limitations of supervised fine-tuning.
contributions: Designs a unified consistency-based training objective that seamlessly bridges offline policy initialization and online reinforcement learning for VLA models.

question: How can pre-trained vision-language models be adapted to generate accurate, spatially relevant 2D paths for robotic manipulation using off-domain data?

source_paper.title: HAMSTER: Hierarchical Action Models For Open-World Robot Manipulation

main_idea.headline: HAMSTER is a hierarchical vision-language-action model that leverages off-domain data by finetuning a high-level VLM to predict coarse 2D paths, which then guide a low-level 3D-aware control policy for robust and generalizable robot manipulation.
contributions: Introduces HAMSTER, a hierarchical vision-language-action architecture that connects a high-level VLM to a low-level 3D policy via 2D end-effector path representations.
Demonstrates that finetuning the high-level VLM on abundant, off-domain data sources like simulations and action-free videos enables strong cross-domain transfer to real-world robotic tasks.
Shows that conditioning low-level 3D policies on VLM-generated 2D paths significantly improves visual and semantic generalization while retaining high-frequency, dexterous control.
Achieves a 50% relative improvement in success rate across seven axes of generalization compared to state-of-the-art monolithic vision-language-action models.

source_paper.problem: Training generalizable robot manipulation policies is bottlenecked by the scarcity and expense of on-robot observation-action data. While monolithic vision-language-action (VLA) models attempt to directly predict actions from images and text, they struggle to generalize beyond their limited training data and are constrained by slow inference speeds, whereas smaller imitation learning policies offer dexterity but lack semantic and visual robustness.

gaps.limitation: Relies on human effort or zero-shot/off-the-shelf VLMs for trajectory generation, which results in lower accuracy and generalization compared to finetuned models.

gaps.target_relation: HAMSTER finetunes its high-level VLM on diverse off-domain data (like simulation and action-free videos) to produce more robust and accurate 2D paths.

gaps.target_relation: HAMSTER utilizes a 3D-aware low-level control policy that incorporates proprioceptive data to improve manipulation robustness.

source_paper.title: IndexTTS: An Industrial-Level Controllable and Efficient Zero-Shot Text-To-Speech System

main_idea.headline: IndexTTS is an industrial-level, zero-shot text-to-speech system that enhances hybrid TTS architectures with a conformer-based conditional encoder, a BigVGAN2 decoder, and character-pinyin hybrid modeling for precise pronunciation control.

source_paper.title: Stacked Intelligent Metasurface Enabled Near-Field Multiuser Beamfocusing in the Wave Domain

main_idea.headline: A novel Stacked Intelligent Metasurface (SIM) architecture is integrated into the base station of a multiuser near-field system to perform wave-domain beamfocusing, replacing conventional digital baseband processing to reduce hardware cost and computational complexity.
contributions: Introduces a SIM-aided multiuser multiple-input single-output near-field communication framework that leverages spherical wavefront characteristics for joint computing and communication.
Incorporates a practical coupled phase and amplitude impedance model to accurately characterize the diffraction behavior of the meta-atoms.
Develops an iterative gradient descent algorithm to optimize the coupled SIM diffraction coefficients by minimizing the normalized mean square error against a target interference-free channel.

source_paper.problem: Extremely large-scale antenna arrays and terahertz communications expand the near-field region, requiring spherical wavefront modeling that complicates channel estimation and beamfocusing. Mitigating inter-user interference in these near-field multiuser systems typically relies on fully digital beamfocusing, which demands a dedicated radio-frequency chain for each antenna and incurs prohibitive hardware costs and computational complexity at the base station. Furthermore, existing single-layer intelligent surfaces lack the signal processing depth to replace digital baseband architectures, while prior multi-layer designs ignore near-field effects and the practical coupled impedance responses of meta-atoms.

gaps.target_relation: The target paper develops a SIM-aided multiuser near-field communication (NFC) system that explicitly considers the diffraction behavior of meta-atoms.

gaps.limitation: The SIM architecture in the cited work necessitates an additional power amplifier factor to offset signal loss during layer penetration.
gaps.evidence_quote: the SIM in [THIS_PAPER] [arXiv_2024_Hao_Multi] required an extra power amplifier factor to compensate for the penetration loss.
gaps.target_relation: The target paper proposes a more comprehensive system model for joint computing and communication to address these practical hardware and propagation constraints.

question: How can the signal radiation and power coupling among multiple pinching antennas on a single waveguide be accurately modeled using physics-based principles to replace idealized identical-power assumptions?

source_paper.title: Modeling and Beamforming Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems

main_idea.headline: This paper establishes a physics-based signal model for Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS) and develops joint transmit and pinching beamforming algorithms to minimize transmit power in multi-user networks.
contributions: A physics-based hardware model that characterizes the electromagnetic coupling between dielectric waveguides and pinching antennas using coupled-mode theory.
A signal model capturing the power coupling effect among multiple pinching antennas on a single waveguide, along with practical equal and proportional power distribution schemes.
A joint transmit and pinching beamforming optimization formulation to minimize transmit power under both continuous and discrete antenna activation constraints.
Two optimization algorithms to solve the multimodal beamforming problem: a penalty-based alternating optimization method and a low-complexity zero-forcing approach.
Empirical demonstration that PASS reduces transmit power by over 95% compared to conventional and massive MIMO systems.

source_paper.problem: Conventional multi-antenna systems and flexible-antenna technologies struggle to fundamentally overcome severe free-space pathloss and line-of-sight blockage, and they lack the ability to reconfigure the antenna array structure after deployment. While the emerging Pinching-Antenna System (PASS) offers a promising near-wired alternative to address these issues, existing theoretical studies rely on non-physical assumptions about signal radiation and are limited to simplified single-user or single-waveguide scenarios, hindering the practical design and optimization of large-scale PASS networks.

question: How can model-derived confidence scores be normalized and utilized in a weighted majority vote to reduce the computational cost of self-consistency decoding?

source_paper.title: Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs

main_idea.headline: Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency (CISC) enhances standard self-consistency decoding by using model-derived confidence scores in a weighted majority vote, significantly reducing computational costs while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: Proposes Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency (CISC), a decoding strategy that performs a confidence-weighted majority vote to achieve comparable accuracy to standard self-consistency with significantly fewer sampled reasoning paths.

Introduces the Within-Question Discrimination (WQD) metric to evaluate confidence scores, showing that standard between-question calibration metrics fail to predict a model's ability to distinguish correct from incorrect answers to the same question.
Provides empirical and qualitative evidence that large language models possess an intrinsic ability to self-assess the correctness of their own reasoning paths.

question: How can 3D occupancy grids be integrated into autonomous driving models to preserve three-dimensional spatial integrity and avoid the reconstruction quality loss associated with 2D projections?

source_paper.title: Occ-LLM: Enhancing Autonomous Driving with Occupancy-Based Large Language Models

main_idea.headline: Occ-LLM is a pioneering occupancy-based Large Language Model for autonomous driving that efficiently integrates 3D occupancy grids using a novel motion separation autoencoder.
contributions: Introduces Occ-LLM, an occupancy-based large language model that enhances spatial and semantic scene comprehension in autonomous driving.

Proposes the Motion Separation Variational Autoencoder (MS-VAE) to manage large volumes of occupancy data by distinguishing between movable and immovable elements, mitigating category imbalance and memory issues.
Formulates a unified framework capable of performing 4D occupancy scene forecasting, self-ego planning, and occupancy-based scene question answering.
Demonstrates strong generalization by seamlessly integrating with and enhancing existing vision-based occupancy prediction algorithms.

source_paper.problem: Although Large Language Models show promise in autonomous driving, existing methods primarily rely on 2D image inputs that lack comprehensive 3D spatial perception. 3D occupancy grids offer a robust alternative by representing both foreground and background elements, but directly integrating them into LLMs is computationally prohibitive due to severe category imbalances and the overwhelming predominance of empty 'air' voxels, which leads to inefficient learning and memory bottlenecks.

source_paper.title: TripoSG: High-Fidelity 3D Shape Synthesis using Large-Scale Rectified Flow Models

main_idea.headline: A large-scale rectified flow transformer paradigm generates high-fidelity 3D meshes with precise alignment to input images by leveraging meticulously curated, large-scale data.
